Package dev.px.core.render

Class Render

java.lang.Object
dev.px.core.render.Render
public final class Render extends Object
The global drawing entry point.

Every module, HUD element and GUI component draws through these static methods. Which library actually executes them is decided once, at startup, by whichever Render2D and Render3D the adapter installs, so swapping NanoVG for Skija is a one-line change that touches no drawing code. 


 Render.roundRect(x, y, w, h, 4, theme.getSurface());
 Render.text("Kill Aura", x + 4, y + 3, Color.WHITE);
 Render.boxOutline(target.getHitbox(), 1.5f, Color.RED);

Before a backend is installed every call is a silent no-op rather than a crash, so a module that draws during early startup is harmless.

    • scaled

      public static void scaled(float originX, float originY, float factor, Runnable body)
      Scales everything drawn by body about the given origin.

      The paired push and pop are easy to unbalance by hand, and an unbalanced transform corrupts every later draw call in the frame. Passing the body in makes that impossible.

    • hasFont

      public static boolean hasFont()
      Returns:
      whether text drawn through the no-font overloads will appear.

      Text calls with no default font installed are dropped, and measurements return zero, rather than throwing. That keeps the documented contract that drawing before a backend exists is harmless, and lets a HUD element size itself from text during early startup without a guard. FontService already warns once when no provider is installed, so the misconfiguration is still reported.
